jobs.title: Financial Analyst, Employee Benefits
jobs.jd: Come join our team! There are many reasons why EPIC Insurance Brokers & Consultants has become one of the fastest-growing firms in the insurance industry. Fueled and driven by capable, committed people who share common beliefs and values and “bring it” every day, EPIC is always looking for people who have “the right stuff” – people who know what they want and aren’t afraid to make it happen. Headquartered in New York City and founded in 2007, our company has over 4,000 employees nationwide. With locations spread out across the U.S., our local market knowledge and industry expertise helps support our clients' regional and global needs. We have grown very quickly since our founding, and we continue to see growth and success thanks to our hard-working and growth-minded employees. Our core values are: Owner mindset, Inspire trust, Think big, and Drive results. If these values and growth align with what you're looking for in your next career? Then consider joining our amazing team! LOCATION : This is a hybrid role for our Duluth, GA location. JOB OVERVIEW: Responsible for developing accurate and timely financial analysis for clients. Prepare various financial and quantitative analysis in support of Client Teams. Employ effective project management skills for balancing requests from multiple Client Teams and for the efficient delivery of results. Requires effective communication skills for clearly explaining detailed analysis to Client Teams and Clients, and the ability to understand Client Teams/Client perspectives that can be reflected in the development of deliverables. WHAT YOU’LL DO: Support Employee Benefit Account Teams • Develop and review monthly reporting for assigned clients • Prepare IBNR (Incurred But Not Reported) analysis • Produce underwriting analysis for client renewals and projections • Produce data warehouse-based reports to support plan performance analysis for clients • Support Client Team strategy initiatives with evaluation of plan design alternatives, rate or employee contribution alternatives, risk profiles, benchmarking, data analytics, vendor change analyses, or program implementation or elimination (financial or quantifiable impact) • Coordinate with vendors as needed to obtain necessary data for analysis New Business Development • Participate in new business activities and meetings as requested WHAT YOU’LL BRING: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent educational training or business experience • College degree in insurance, risk management, math or related field preferred • Aptitude for performing financial analysis for a benefits consulting or brokerage firm (we will provide training). KSAs (Knowledge, Skills, Abilities) • Microsoft Office Suite experience including large data sets • Able to effectively interface with internal and external customers • Able to handle confidential information with maximum discretion • Able to understand business principles and apply them accordingly • Able to work independently and on a team within a fast-paced, deadline driven environment • Career-focused • Demonstrate good judgment while managing projects, multi-tasking, prioritizing, and meeting deadlines with a sense of urgency • Detail-oriented, organized, efficient, and proactive • Excellent written/verbal communication skills including communicating complex financial information • High level of accountability and flexibility • High-touch client orientation • Open and willing to receive and give constructive critique • Strong analytical and quantitative skills Special Requirements • Flexible to work outside normal working hours COMPENSATION: Compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, skills, training, certifications, education, internal equity, and market data. This role may also be eligible for bonuses and a comprehensive benefits package. WHY EPIC: EPIC has over 60 offices and 4,000 employees nationwide – and we’re growing! It’s a great time to join the team and be a part of this growth. We offer: Generous Paid Time off Managed PTO for salaried/exempt employees (personal time off without accruals or caps); 22 PTO days starting out for hourly/non-exempt employees; 12 company-observed paid holidays; 4 early-close days Generous leave time options: Paid parental leave, pregnancy disability and bonding leave, and organ donor/bone marrow donor leave Generous employee referral bonus program of $1,500 per hired referral Employee recognition programs for demonstrating EPIC’s values plus additional employee recognition awards and programs (and trips!) Employee Resource Groups: Women’s Coalition, EPIC Veterans Group Professional growth & development: Mentorship Program, Tuition Reimbursement Program, Leadership Development Unique benefits such as Pet Insurance, Identity Theft & Fraud Protection Coverage, Legal Planning, Family Planning, and Menopause & Midlife Support Additional benefits include (but are not limited to): 401(k) matching, medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, and wellness & employee assistance programs 50/50 Work Culture: EPIC fosters a 50/50 culture between producers and the rest of the business, supporting collaboration, teamwork, and an inclusive work environment. It takes both production and service to be EPIC! EPIC Gives Back – Some of our charitable efforts include Donation Connection, Employee Assistance Fund, and People First Foundation We’re in the top 10 of property/casualty agencies according to “Insurance Journal” To learn more about EPIC, visit our Careers Page: https://www.epicbrokers.com/about/epic-careers/ . EPIC embraces diversity in all its various forms—whether it be diversity of thought, background, race, religion, gender, skills or experience. We are committed to fostering a work community where every colleague feels welcomed, valued, respected and heard. It is our belief that diversity drives innovation and that creating an environment where every employee feels included and empowered, helps us to deliver the best outcome to our clients. California Applicants - View your privacy rights at: https://www.epicbrokers.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/epic-ca-employee-privacy-notice.pdf . jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.jd:
Why We Exist

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey — buy/sell, insurance, maintenance, repairs — is fragmented, complicated, and expensive.

Jerry.ai http://Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all. We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top 3 brokers in the U.S., then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace. 

We've reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, scaled revenue 70X, and became profitable in early 2024. We're now expanding into adjacent verticals (e.g. home, motorcycle, RV, etc) to become the one-stop-shop for all your physical assets.



Why We’re Hiring

Our Data Science & Analytics team has been a force multiplier and accelerant to our business that has helped us reach these pivotal milestones in spite of headwinds and within a highly competitive market. They are a team of former McKinsey, BCG and Bain consultants who drive data & insights, and inform decision-making across every corner of our business. They are analytical powerhouses and first principles problem solvers who push forward our most important initiatives across product, growth, tech, and operations.

Every business unit has a Data Science team member embedded within it  —  someone who doesn't just run analyses and build dashboards, but shapes what questions we should ask, what data to pull, what conclusions to draw, what decisions to make, and then drives our teams towards our next goal: go from 5M to 50M customers and become a $10B business in the next 4 years. 

 

As our business continues to expand, there is growing demand for more Data Science team members. We are hiring 2-3 people to drive impact in these areas:

 - Growth Marketing 

 - Product Development

 - AI & Automation

 - Strategic Partnerships 

 

On leveling: You may see job ads for this role at different job levels. Our priority is finding the right people, we can be flexible with job title/leveling.



Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here

 - No slides: If you've worked in consulting, you know what it feels like to be up at 3am reformatting a deck. That doesn't exist here. The only work that gets done at Jerry is work that will materially change the trajectory of our business — an important product, a new growth channel, a key metric, a critical partner relationship, etc. 

 - No corporate fluff: The Data Science & Analytics team is 14 insatiable learners who care deeply about solving difficult problems and making a tangible impact. Every person owns a critical domain. There is no bloat, unnecessary meetings, or waiting for approvals. 

 - Hands-on: This is not a pure strategy role, you will also own execution. Your day-to-day will be surfacing analytical insights, driving decisions, and seeing them through end-to-end. 



What You'll Own

You'll sit on our central Data Science & Analytics team but you’ll be embedded in one of Jerry's core business areas — growth, product, AI and automation, strategic partnerships — and own the analytical function for that business unit end-to-end.

 - Define the right problems: Before any analysis, understand what business question it's answering and what decision it will inform. Push back if the question is flawed.

 - Data and insights: Define metrics, build reports, run analyses, design experiments, and surface data insights that move your team's key metrics.

 - Drive outcomes: Bring recommendations to your counterparts in product, growth, finance or operations, tell them what's happening and why, and what next steps should be.

 

Who You Are

 - First principles thinker: You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses before touching data. You're analytically strong (comfortable with SQL or Python) but your instinct is to ask "what are we trying to solve here?" before jumping to "what should I build?" 

 - Direct communicator: You can walk a skeptical stakeholder through a complex finding and get buy-in quickly. You write clearly, speak precisely, and don't bury the lede.

 - Owner: You act like your name is on the door. If something is broken, you feel responsible for fixing it, even if it’s outside of your swim lane.

 

What You'll Bring

 - 2+ years of experience at a consulting firm, investment bank, or high-growth technology company.

 - Strong analytical skills; ability to pull, structure, and interpret data independently.

 - Track record of owning ambiguous problems and delivering impact.

 - Clear, persuasive communicator who can influence decisions at the leadership level.

 

Our Tools

SQL (Clickhouse), Metabase, Python, Jupyter Hub, GitHub.

 
 

While we appreciate your interest and application, due to the volume of applications we receive, only applicants under consideration will be contacted.

jobs.title: Data Scientist - Credit (Retros)
jobs.jd:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.


ABOUT THE TEAM

We’re part of Plaid’s Data organization, building models and insights that help millions of people better understand and grow their financial lives. We use Plaid’s unique financial data to help lenders make more informed decisions and build better credit experiences.

We partner across data science, engineering, product, and Go-to-Market to turn complex data into practical customer recommendations and scalable solutions. We value technical rigor, creativity, user empathy, and teamwork.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on the Credit team, you’ll apply quantitative analysis and deep credit expertise to help lenders make better use of cash flow insights. You’ll work across customer problems, credit policy, and data products—translating Plaid’s data into recommendations and insights that drive business impact and inform product direction.

Your day-to-day responsibilities may include:

 - Deep-dive into model performance for clients, triage issues, and identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

 - Analyze Plaid’s unique data to identify emerging credit risk signals and build and evaluate credit retrospectives.

 - Create tailored recommendations for clients based on their data and Plaid’s insights.

 - Build and maintain data pipelines, including ETL processes using tools such as dbt.

 - Develop metrics, alerts, and dashboards to monitor production machine learning model performance.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the process of developing hands-on recommendations for incorporating cash flow insights into lending decisions, using best practices for account-level decisioning.

 - Improve customer adoption of Plaid Insights through custom analysis tailored to each customer’s needs.

 - Serve as a subject matter expert on credit insights and credit policy implementation, supporting Data Science, Engineering, and Go-to-Market partners.

 - Apply your expertise in quantitative analysis, data mining, and data visualization to develop models and actionable insights.

 - Identify useful signals that can inform machine learning models.

 - Inform and influence Product and Engineering teams through clear analysis and presentations.



WHAT EXCITES YOU

 - Applying data science and credit expertise to real-world lending decisions.

 - Working with Plaid’s unique financial data to uncover emerging credit risk signals and create useful customer insights.

 - Helping lenders make more informed decisions with cash flow data and account-level recommendations.

 - Partnering across Data Science, Engineering, Product, and Go-to-Market to turn analysis into customer and product impact.

 - Working on high-impact problems that can improve financial access and outcomes.



WHAT EXCITES US

 - 2–5 years of industry experience in a financial services Data Science role.

 - Deep familiarity with SQL and Python.

 - Deep understanding of credit risk and the development of underwriting models.

 - Hands-on credit expertise building and maintaining credit policies for lenders.

 - Knowledge of the lending lifecycle and how to optimize each step, including marketing, acquisition, customer management, and collections or recoveries.

 - Demonstrated ability to make data-driven decisions.

 - Nice to have: Experience building data pipelines and automating ETL processes with dbt or similar tools.

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!



Plaid is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religion or religious belief, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, military or veteran status, disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Plaid is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need any assistance with your application or interviews due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations@plaid.com.



Please review our Candidate Privacy Notice here https://plaid.com/legal/#candidate-privacy-notice.


Additional compensation in the form(s) of equity and/or commission are dependent on the position offered. Plaid provides a comprehensive benefit plan, including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k). Pay is based on factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience and skillset, and location. Pay and benefits are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefit plans.

jobs.title: Quant Risk Analyst - Derivatives & Clearing
jobs.jd:
ABOUT POLYMARKET

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform, where people trade on the outcomes of real-world events. As our markets, volumes, and derivative product suite grow, so does the sophistication of the risk infrastructure behind them. Our clearing and risk systems must operate with the rigor of a traditional clearinghouse while moving at the speed of a crypto-native trading platform.


THE ROLE

We're hiring a mid-level quantitative risk analyst to design and implement enterprise-scale risk models at the heart of our clearing operation. You'll own models for market risk, volatility and correlation of derivatives, stress testing, and automated liquidation — the systems that keep the platform solvent and users protected in fast-moving markets.

This is a hands-on role: you'll be building models in production code, not just specifying them. We expect you to work fluently with AI tools for development and research — and to be the skeptic in the room, pressure-testing AI-generated models and code against well-established risk frameworks before anything ships.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design, implement, and maintain enterprise-scale risk models covering market risk, margin, and counterparty exposure for a clearing organization.

 - Build volatility and correlation models for derivatives, including calibration, backtesting, and ongoing model validation.

 - Develop and run stress-testing frameworks: historical scenarios, hypothetical shocks, and reverse stress tests.

 - Design and tune auto-liquidation logic — trigger thresholds, liquidation waterfalls, and safeguards against cascading liquidations.

 - Use AI tools extensively to accelerate model development, coding, and research — and rigorously validate AI outputs against established risk models (VaR/ES, SPAN-style margining, GARCH-family volatility models, standard correlation frameworks) before deployment.

 - Monitor model performance in production, investigate breaks, and iterate quickly.

 - Partner with engineering, trading, and product teams to embed risk controls into platform architecture.

 - Document model assumptions, limitations, and validation results to an audit-ready standard.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5–7 years of quantitative risk experience at a clearinghouse, exchange, prime broker, trading firm, or similar.

 - Proven expertise designing and implementing risk models at enterprise scale — production systems, not just research prototypes.

 - Deep experience modeling volatility, correlation, option skews, option pricing and implementing at scale for trad-fi derivatives, perpetuals, and fully collateralized event contracts.

 - Hands-on experience with market risk modeling, stress testing, and auto-liquidation mechanics in a clearing context.

 - Strong fluency with AI-assisted development and coding, paired with the judgment to pressure-test AI outputs against well-established risk models and catch what looks plausible but is wrong.

 - Expert-level Python (numerical stack: NumPy, pandas, SciPy; solid software engineering practices).

 - Advanced degree in a quantitative field (math, statistics, physics, financial engineering, CS) or equivalent experience.

 - Strong mathematical foundation in stochastic calculus and linear algebra.


NICE TO HAVE

 - C# and/or C++ for performance-critical or production systems.

 - Familiarity with crypto market structure, perpetuals, or prediction markets.

 - Experience with CCP risk frameworks (CPMI-IOSCO PFMI, default management, margin methodology).

 - Experience building real-time risk systems.


PAY TRANSPARENCY

Base salary range: $400,000 to $450,000, plus equity and benefits.

This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.


LOCATION & WORK SETUP

This role is based in our New York City office, in person. You'll be working directly alongside the trading, engineering, and risk teams.

This role will partner with commercial, analytics, technology, and senior stakeholders to modernize reporting workflows, improve reporting quality, and deliver scalable BI solutions that support business decision-making. About the team- Elsevier’s Healthcare Education team develops digital learning, assessment, and simulation products—including Sherpath AI, ClinicalKey Student, Shadow Health, HESI, Complete Anatomy, and Osmosis—to support medical and nursing students, educators, and future healthcare professionals worldwide. From an AI Software Engineering perspective, the team’s work spans generative AI, RAG, intelligent search, personalized learning, data analytics, cloud-based applications, and virtual patient simulations to improve educational experiences and learning outcomes. Key Responsibilities Owning the development and enhancement of Trade and Commercial Reporting solutions across Snowflake, Tableau, and related BI environments. Applying AI tools, where appropriate, to improve analysis, documentation, workflow efficiency, and reporting development. Converting legacy manual reporting workflows, including Excel-based processes, into scalable dashboards, automated reporting, and repeatable analytical solutions. Supporting reporting migrations by translating legacy queries, business rules, and reporting logic into new data warehouse environments. Validating reporting outputs across legacy and new environments to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with business definitions. Partnering with commercial stakeholders, including senior and VP-level audiences, to gather requirements, clarify business questions, and deliver actionable reporting outputs. Investigating data discrepancies, perform quality checks, document issues, and coordinating resolution with business and technical partners. Managing multiple reporting priorities and stakeholder requests with strong attention to detail and limited oversight. jobs.title: Data Scientist II
jobs.jd: At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business. Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work. Join us and build for travelers everywhere. Data Scientist II Expedia Group is looking for a Data Scientist II to help improve the post-booking experience for travelers. You will use data analysis, experimentation, and statistical methods to answer product and service questions, understand performance, and help teams make evidence-based decisions. Working with experienced data scientists and cross-functional partners, you will take analytical work from a clearly framed question through findings and recommendations. In this role you will: Analyze traveler servicing and service-platform data to identify trends, explain performance changes, and uncover opportunities to improve experiences and operations. Build and maintain analyses, dashboards, and recurring metrics that help partners understand service health and outcomes. Support the design and evaluation of experiments, including metric selection, data validation, interpretation, and clear communication of results. Apply statistical techniques and exploratory analysis to investigate product questions and assess the likely impact of proposed changes. Use SQL and a programming language such as Python or R to work with data, automate repeatable analyses, and document your methods. Partner with product, engineering, operations, and analytics teammates to clarify questions, share findings, and help translate insights into next steps. Present analytical results in a clear, concise way, explaining assumptions, limitations, and implications for non-technical audiences. Contribute to reliable analytical practices, including data quality checks, reproducible work, and consistent metric definitions. Experience and Qualifications: Experience applying analytics, data science, statistics, or a related discipline to business or product questions. Working proficiency in SQL and Python, R, or a similar analytical programming language. Foundational knowledge of statistical analysis, hypothesis testing, and experimental design. Experience exploring datasets, validating results, and communicating findings with charts, dashboards, or written narratives. Ability to break down a defined problem, manage analytical tasks, and seek feedback when assumptions or requirements are unclear. Curiosity, attention to detail, and collaborative communication skills. You have a bachelor's, master's, or Ph.D. degree in a quantitative, scientific, or related technical field; or equivalent related professional experience. Helpful experience Three or more years of experience working with e-commerce and/or clickstream data. Exposure to product analytics, digital experimentation, customer support, travel, self-service, or post-booking customer journeys. Familiarity with data visualization tools, cloud data platforms, and version-controlled analytical workflows. Exposure to predictive modeling or machine-learning methods and interest in applying them to customer or operational problems. Why this role You’ll help teams improve servicing by turning data into useful insights and stronger decisions. The work supports the team’s focus on rigorous experimentation, understanding end-to-end service-platform health, and applying machine learning to optimize processes and drive business outcomes. #LI-MC1 The total cash range for this position in Seattle is $112,000.00 to $156,500.00. jobs.title: Graduate Analyst
jobs.jd: Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money. Min fees. Max ease. Full speed. Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money. As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money. For everyone, everywhere. More about our mission and what we offer . As a Graduate Product Analyst, you’ll join our North America Regional Analytics team in September 2027. This full-time role is a chance to make a real impact early and kickstart your career. You’ll be onboarded with the global Graduate cohort in one of our offices and learn the basics of being a Wiser. The Role: We’re hiring three graduates to work as analysts inside our North America product teams, which build Wise for personal and business customers in the US and Canada. Our analysts don’t sit in a central reporting team: each one works day to day with product managers & engineers and helps them decide what to build next and whether it worked. You’ll join one of four teams: Onboarding, Send, Account or Growth. Each owns a different stage of the customer’s journey with Wise, and each is described below. You won’t be on your own. A senior analyst will mentor you, review your work and help you grow, and you’ll be part of a team of analysts covering the whole North America product. What you’ll be doing: Shape Strategy & Prioritization: You’ll help your team understand where customers struggle and what is worth fixing first. That means digging into funnels and customer behavior, reading customer feedback and survey responses, and sizing opportunities so the team can prioritize the work with the biggest impact. As you grow, you’ll lead your own discoveries and present recommendations to your product manager. Learn Launch Rigor & Experimentation: You’ll help design and analyze A/B tests and pre/post comparisons for new features, and learn to turn the results into a clear call: roll out, iterate or roll back. You’ll keep an eye on your team’s core metrics and flag when something looks wrong. Build on the Semantic Layer: We believe analysts add the most value when they focus on product discovery, not ad-hoc requests. You’ll learn to build and maintain the data models and dashboards that let your team answer their own questions, using Snowflake, dbt, Git, Airflow, Python and Lightdash, and help improve the AI skills that run our routine reporting. Share What You Learn: You’ll explain your findings to your team and the wider NorthAm squad, in writing, in charts and in person, so that your work leads to a decision. How we work with AI: We lean hard into AI: AI skills produce our routine work and deep dives, so our analysts can focus on discovery. You’ll use AI tools every day, and you’ll own the answer, not the tool: checking the data, the logic and the conclusion before anyone acts on it. Where you could join: Onboarding Onboarding owns the first steps of a customer’s journey: creating a profile, getting verified (Know Your Customer / Know Your Business checks) and taking a first action with Wise. It also keeps financial crime out at the front door. The core challenge is letting genuine customers through quickly while stopping bad actors. You might work on questions like: Where do new customers drop out between signing up and their first transfer, and what would bring them back? Which verification steps slow genuine customers down without catching more fraud or financial crime? Send Send covers what happens when a customer sends money, and is made up of three teams: Pay-in: how customers pay money into Wise, for example by bank transfer (ACH) or card. Which payment methods help customers complete their transfer, and what does each one cost us? Payout: how money reaches recipients’ bank accounts in the US and Canada, balancing three levers: cost, speed and conversion. What would make these payouts faster or cheaper, and how much more volume would that bring? You’ll also help track the health of our banking partners. Payment Risk: transfer suspensions and ACH and card chargebacks. How do we cut losses from chargebacks and fraud without blocking good customers? Account Account owns how customers use Wise as an account, not only for one-off transfers: getting paid into Wise with USD and CAD local account details, spending with the Wise debit card, and earning a return on money held with Wise. You might work on questions like: What makes a customer start getting paid into their Wise account, and what makes them keep doing it? Who uses the Wise card, for what, and what stops others from using it? Does holding money with Wise change how customers send money abroad? Growth Growth owns the top of the funnel: how people find Wise and decide to try it. That covers landing pages, the promotion engine, corridor strategy (which country-to-country routes we focus on) and pricing, where you’ll work with our Pricing Data Science team to understand how price affects demand. You might work on questions like: Did a promotion bring in customers who stay, or customers who leave once it ends? Which corridors should we focus on next, and why? Your first six months: By three months: you own part of your team’s regular metrics and have delivered your first analysis. By six months: you’ve led a discovery or an experiment readout from question to recommendation and presented it to your team. Qualifications What you’ll bring: Education: A bachelor’s or master’s degree in a quantitative field such as economics, statistics, mathematics, computer science or engineering, completed by your start date, or equivalent practical experience. Technical Foundations: You’ve used SQL, Python or R to answer a real question with data, in a course, a project, an internship or on your own. You understand the basics of statistics, such as distributions, hypothesis tests and confidence intervals, and can tell when a difference is real rather than noise. Curiosity & Product Sense: You want to know why customers behave the way they do, and you ask “so what should we do?” about every result. Clear Communication: You can explain a finding to someone who isn’t technical, in writing and in conversation, and you’re comfortable saying “I don’t know yet”. Ownership: You finish what you start, ask for help early and act on feedback. AI with Judgment: You use AI tools to work faster, and you check their output before you trust it. Right to Work: You must be authorized to work in the US. We’re unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Nice to have but not essential: Hands-on experience with any of Snowflake, dbt, Git, Airflow or Lightdash. Exposure to A/B testing or causal inference, in a course or in practice. An internship or project in analytics, data science, product or finance. An interest in payments, fintech, or how people move and manage money across borders. For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive. We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences. Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers. If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs . Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram .

jobs.title: Economist, Macro & Economic Insights
jobs.jd:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.



The Economics Team uses economic research and data science to deepen our understanding of economic, credit, and financial trends. We combine rigorous empirical analysis with clear communication to inform decisions across and beyond Plaid.



You will conduct applied economic research, develop reliable analytical methods, and turn complex findings into clear, useful insights. Working with economists and data scientists, you will own research projects from question framing and data preparation through validation and written communication. This is a hands-on role for an economist who enjoys working with large datasets, exercising sound judgment, and explaining evidence and limitations to a range of audiences. You will have opportunities to develop a research specialty and take on broader ownership as the team grows.



We're guided by our principles including impact, growing together, embracing openness and positivity, and inventing tomorrow; we're looking for leaders who are motivated by those same principles






Responsibilities

 - Investigating economic questions and trends through rigorous empirical research, from framing the question through analysis, validation, and communication

 - Working with large, complex datasets to develop reliable measures and reproducible analytical workflows

 - Evaluating findings against established research and public benchmarks, assessing data quality and representativeness, and clearly communicating uncertainty and limitations

 - Applying econometric and time-series methods to test hypotheses, assess robustness, and distinguish meaningful patterns from noise

 - Writing clear research briefs and presenting findings to technical and nontechnical audiences; partnering with colleagues across research, data science, and the business to identify useful questions and inform decisions






Qualifications

 - PhD in economics or a related empirical field, or a Master's plus 4+ years of relevant applied experience, with strong empirical training. Exceptional candidates completing their PhD in 2027 are welcome; relevant research includes applied macroeconomics, household or behavioral finance, fintech, and financial regulation

 - Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience independently analyzing large, complex datasets and building reproducible analytical workflows

 - Strong econometric and time-series modeling skills, with experience applying these methods to economic questions and assessing robustness

 - Excellent writing for non-academic audiences, demonstrated through policy memos, market commentary, or research briefs. You can explain and defend your methods, findings, and limitations to technical and nontechnical audiences

 - Sound research judgment: you distinguish evidence from interpretation, communicate uncertainty, and scope claims to what the data supports

 - Nice to have: experience conducting applied economic research in fintech, finance, a research institute, or a public-sector organization; prior ownership of a recurring research publication

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

jobs.title: Revenue Strategy & Operations
jobs.jd:
ABOUT ELEVENLABS

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

 - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.




HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We’re looking for someone to join our team in Revenue Strategy & Operations and play a key role in scaling our go-to-market operations. This role is at the intersection of technical problem-solving and operational excellence, focusing on building and maintaining tools, automations, and dashboards that empower our sales, data, and product teams to execute with precision.

As part of the Revenue Operations team, you'll collaborate across functions to design and implement systems that streamline sales processes, enhance decision-making, and drive growth. The GTM Strategy and Operations team operates as strategic advisors to key cross-functional partners, podded by functional area (pre- vs. post-sale) to drive revenue acceleration, insights, and business growth. This is an exciting opportunity to bring technical and analytical expertise to a fast-paced, impactful environment.

Each Revenue Strategy & Operations team member serves as a dedicated partner to a specific go-to-market function, whether that's SDRs, AEs, Partnerships, or Account Management.

In this role, you will be responsible for:

 - E2E Process Management - Build and maintain strategic automations and standardized processes that support cross-functional teams and promote consistency and adoption.

 - Cross-Functional Collaboration - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive initiatives that enhance revenue generation and operational effectiveness.

 - Leadership Partnership - Serve as a trusted partner to leadership, providing strategic insights, actionable recommendations, and performance reporting.

 - Experimentation - Develop and test new ideas, workflows, and sources that improve critical levers within each functional area.

 - Data-Driven Strategy - Oversee analytics and performance analyses across their associated functions. Identify areas of opportunity and acceleration; build dashboards and insights that inform experimentation and guide lever improvement.

 - Reporting & Analytics - Lead the design and management of dashboards, reports, and key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure and enhance team performance.

Who you are

We're looking for exceptional individuals who combine technical excellence with ethical awareness, who are excited by hard problems and motivated by human impact. You’ll strive with us if you:



 - Are passionate about audio AI driven by a desire to make content universally accessible and breaking the frontiers of new tech.

 - Are a highly motivated and driven individual with a strong work ethic. Our team is aware of this critical moment of audio AI evolution and is committed to going the extra mile to lead.

 - Are analytical, efficient, and strive on solving complex challenges with a first principles mindset.

 - Consistently strive for excellence, delivering high-quality work quickly and exceeding expectations.

 - Take initiative and work autonomously from day one, prioritizing learning and contribution while leaving ego aside.

What you bring

 - 4+ years of Revenue Operations at high-growth technology companies

 - Proven track record of developing and implementing end-to-end solutions, from data collection and analysis to execution.

 - Can break complex problems into smaller, actionable solution steps

 - Strong analytical skills, with proven expertise in SQL and data visualization using BI tools (e.g. Sigma)

 - Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams.

 - Highly adaptable, with a proactive approach to problem-solving and process improvement.

 - Strong coachability and willingness to learn and adapt to new challenges.



What we offer

 - High-velocity innovation: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - A truly global team: Collaboration with teammates across 30+ countries, a global customer footprint and office hubs in New York, London and Warsaw. Annual company offsite for the whole team to get together (the last one in Croatia!)

 - Remote first: We prioritize your talent, not your location, with structured asynchronous workflows for maximum impact and minimal meetings.

 - Continuous growth: Collaborate with AI leaders, shape your path, and contribute where you excel most.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer
jobs.jd:
Who We Are

Ontic provides software that helps corporate and government security teams identify threats, assess risk, and respond faster to keep people and organizations safe. Its AI-powered Connected Intelligence Platform unifies security operations and data into a centralized system of record, enabling organizations to conduct risk assessments, protect against workplace violence, and manage threats and incidents more efficiently. Fortune 500 companies and federal agencies rely on Ontic to support security programs such as executive protection, threat intelligence, and corporate investigations. Learn more at ontic.ai http://ontic.ai or follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/ontic-technologies/.

Who You Are
We are hiring a dedicated Analytics Engineer to help build and scale the data and AI foundation of our enterprise SaaS business.

Reporting to the Sr. Director of AI & Analytics within our centralized Operations organization, this is a highly hands-on role focused on architecting scalable analytics systems and AI-enabled workflows that power decision-making across the company.

You will design the core data models, architecture, and reusable assets that serve Product, Engineering & Design — while helping redefine what an analytics function looks like in the age of AI.

This is a foundational hire with high ownership and long-term growth potential.

What You'll Do

1. Enterprise Data Modeling & Architecture

 - Design and maintain scalable dbt data models in Snowflake that serve as trusted sources of truth across the business

 - Architect data pipelines and transformation workflows using Fivetran and modern ELT practices

 - Develop durable, extensible data assets that evolve as the company scales

 - Establish modeling standards, documentation practices, and governance frameworks

 - Partner with RevOps and Finance to define and operationalize core SaaS metrics (ARR, retention, expansion, pipeline, etc.)
   

2. AI-Enabled Systems & Workflow Integration

 - Build data foundations that power internal AI applications and LLM-enabled workflows

 - Prototype and productionize AI-driven operational use cases

 - Integrate analytics and AI into everyday workflows using tools such as Notion, Cursor, Glean, and other emerging platforms

 - Design systems that embed data directly into operational processes — not just dashboards
   

3. Cross-Functional Analytics Infrastructure

 - Partner with leaders across Sales, CS, Marketing, Finance, Product, and Engineering to translate business needs into scalable technical systems

 - Create reusable data assets that enable activation via Hightouch and analysis via Omni

 - Ensure architecture is scalable, secure, and adaptable to evolving enterprise requirements
   

Our Stack

Analytics: Fivetran, dbt, Snowflake, Hightouch, Omni
AI & Knowledge Systems: Notion, Cursor, Glean

Experience with these tools is helpful but not required. Strong fundamentals and the ability to quickly learn new technologies matter more than prior tool exposure.



What We’re Looking For

 - 3-6 years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or similar hands-on roles

 - Strong SQL skills and deep understanding of modern data modeling (dimensional modeling, transformations, data contracts, etc.)

 - Experience building in cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, etc.)

 - Comfort working in a fast-moving, evolving AI tooling landscape

 - Systems-level thinker who designs for scalability, extensibility, and flexibility

 - Naturally curious and energized by solving ambiguous problems

 - Pride in building clean, durable architecture — not just shipping quick fixes

 - Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate across business and technical teams

 - Nice to have: Experience with Pendo, Amplitude, Heap, or Mixpanel



Why This Role Matters

We are not building a traditional BI function.

We are building an AI-augmented analytics capability that:

 - Embeds data into operational workflows

 - Enables faster, smarter enterprise decision-making

 - Evolves as AI tooling evolves

 - Treats architecture as a strategic asset, not a back-office utility
   

You won’t just build dashboards — you will help shape how analytics and AI power our company over the next several years.

Develop recurring and ad hoc reports, dashboards, visualizations, and performance metrics to support decision-making and operational improvements. Collect, organize, clean, validate, and maintain data from multiple systems to ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness. Investigate data discrepancies, resolve reporting issues, and collaborate with information technology staff on system updates and improvements. Maintain documentation of data definitions, reporting methods, business rules, and data quality standards. Support accreditation reviews, annual reporting, program assessment, and evaluation of organizational goals and performance measures. jobs.jd: ABOUT FLAGSHIP PIONEERING Flagship Pioneering is a platform innovation company that conceives, creates, resources, and develops first-in-category life sciences and technology companies. Since its founding in 2000, Flagship has originated over 100 scientific ventures and has deployed over $3 billion in capital toward the development of transformative life science businesses. Flagship's current portfolio of more than 35 companies includes Moderna, Generate Biomedicines, Sail Biomedicines, iris labs, and Extuitive. ABOUT FL127 FL127 is a privately held, early-stage company operating within the Flagship Pioneering ecosystem. The company is developing a first-in-category platform anchored in novel device technology. FL127 is building its scientific and technical foundation through a hypothesis-driven experimental program. We are assembling a lean team of scientists and engineers who work at the intersection of hardware, software, and physiology, and who want to build in an era when AI agents are first-class members of the team. THE ROLE FL127 is seeking a scientist to help connect the physiological signals our platform measures to what they indicate about a person. You will ground each signal in physiology, help design the human studies that test what it reflects, and build models that relate our measurements to reference measures and outcomes in small human cohorts. Our imaging and signal-extraction team produces the measurements. Your work starts from those outputs. You will co-design human studies with that team so a single study informs both measurement quality and interpretation. FL127 is an AI-native company. Team members direct AI agents in their daily work for literature synthesis, study design, data analysis, and code. We are looking for someone who wants to work this way. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Ground each measured signal in physiology: what it reflects, what confounds it, and which physiological states it may indicate Work with the product and market team to decide which applications to study first, weighing scientific plausibility, study cost, and user value Co-design human studies with the imaging team, including endpoints, reference measurements, and protocols Build and evaluate models that relate our measurements to reference measures and outcomes on small cohorts, with attention to confounders, leakage, demographic stratification, and sample size Set the evidence bar a finding must meet before it shapes the product, and report what the data supports and where it falls short Review extracted signals for physiological plausibility and suggest improvements to the measurement pipeline REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS PhD in biomedical engineering, physiology, bioengineering, biophotonics, or a related field, or an MD/PhD, with substantial applied machine learning experience Deep knowledge of human physiology in an area such as microcirculation, hemodynamics, tissue optics, skin biology, or cardiorespiratory physiology Experience taking a measurement or digital biomarker through human studies, including endpoint selection, reference measurements, IRB-governed protocols, and agreement analysis Statistical modeling on small human datasets, including within-subject and longitudinal designs Proficiency in Python and the modern ML stack, and comfort working inside an existing research codebase Enough imaging and signal-processing background to reason about how calibration, registration, and sampling affect a derived measurement Ability to work independently in an early-stage, ambiguous environment and make decisions with incomplete data PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Published or applied work in remote physiological sensing, digital biomarkers, or wearable or contactless measurement Experience turning research results into a product feature, ideally at a consumer device company Familiarity with skin optics models (Monte Carlo simulation, diffusion theory, chromophore decomposition) Experience modeling individual baselines and change over time Experience in a venture-backed startup or early-stage research environment WHY FL127 Work with human study data from your first weeks Shape which applications the jobs.title: Data Scientist, Cloud Distribution & Growth
jobs.jd:
About the Team

Cloud service providers give developers a way to use OpenAI models in the environments where they already build and run software. Our team works with Go-to-Market (GTM), Product, Engineering, and Finance to understand which customers we can reach through these providers and what helps them grow from a first API call to a production workload.

About the Role

In your first few months, you’ll identify a customer segment or workload where OpenAI can grow, recommend an investment to GTM, Product, and Engineering, and define how we’ll know whether it brought new usage to OpenAI. Your first priority will be to explain what drives usage and revenue across providers. You’ll use that understanding to help GTM decide which customers and workloads to invest in and to build forecasts the team can plan against.

A customer might sign a substantial cloud commitment and send very little traffic. You can sit down with the account team, trace the customer’s first requests, and work out whether they need help launching, access to a different model, or more capacity. When you see the same opportunity across customers, your work can change where OpenAI invests.

In This Role, You Will:

 - Build a reliable view of the business from provider usage reports, billing records, and API logs. Show how new workloads, expansion, changes in price, and shifts in model mix contribute to growth.

 - Estimate how much demand cloud distribution adds to OpenAI. Trace customer activity across channels to distinguish new use cases from traffic that moved from the direct API.

 - Identify where customers are ready to scale. Combine what account teams hear with evidence on request failures, latency, and model availability. Work with Product and Engineering on a change and measure what happens to usage.

 - Shape growth plans with GTM and Finance. Estimate what existing workloads and upcoming launches can contribute by year end, test the assumptions that matter most, and recommend where to focus with each provider.

 - Own the consumption forecast. Compare forecasts with actual usage over the same period, explain the biggest misses, and use what you learn to improve the next forecast.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Like questions that take you from a conversation with an account team to a query about a single API request. You’re curious about why a customer’s behavior differs from what the numbers first suggest.

 - Are comfortable making a recommendation while some questions are still open. You can tell a sales leader where you’d invest and explain to an engineer what evidence would change your mind.

Qualifications

 - Experience independently leading data science work on a product, growth, or commercial question that changed a business decision.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills. You can join incomplete datasets, choose the right unit of analysis, and validate an aggregate result against individual customers or workloads.

 - Experience using cohorts, experiments, or observational comparisons to assess what drove a change. You can explain how customer selection affects the conclusion and evaluate a forecast against a simple baseline.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience with API platforms, cloud marketplaces, enterprise GTM, or a usage-based business.

 - Experience connecting service reliability or capacity to customer adoption, or using demand forecasts to guide a commercial or infrastructure investment.

The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience managing Personal Information and Contact Information processes, developing and processing EIBs, configuring reference letters and related documents, and supporting large-scale data migration and data validation activities. This role will partner closely with HR, Payroll, Recruiting, Compensation, and IT teams to deliver projects, enhancements, production support, and data initiatives. Key Responsibilities Configure, maintain, and enhance Workday Core HCM, with a strong focus on Personal Information, Contact Information, Staffing, Jobs & Positions, and employee data management. Configure and support Personal Information Business Processes, including routing, approvals, validations, condition rules, notifications, security, and related employee self-service functionality. Create, test, process, and troubleshoot Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB) files for high-volume and mass business transactions. Manage inbound EIB processing, including data preparation, transformation, validation, error resolution, reconciliation, and post-load verification. Support HR data migration and conversion activities, including data extraction, cleansing, mapping, transformation, loading, reconciliation, and validation between legacy systems and Workday. Partner with business and technical teams to define data mapping and conversion requirements and ensure migrated data meets Workday configuration and business requirements. Configure and maintain reference letters, employment letters, document templates, and other employee-related Workday documents, including dynamic fields, calculated fields, conditional content, and business process integration. Perform mass updates and data corrections using appropriate Workday tools while maintaining strong data quality, integrity, and audit controls. Analyze and resolve EIB errors, data discrepancies, validation failures, and other complex Workday data issues. Configure and maintain Workday Business Processes, including BP routing, approvals, condition rules, notifications, validations, questionnaires, documents, and Business Process Security Policies. Support Workday production issues and serve as a Tier escalation contact for complex Core HCM, Personal Information, EIB, document, and data-related issues. Develop and utilize Workday reports and calculated fields to support data validation, reconciliation, migration, troubleshooting, and business requirements. Support testing activities, including unit testing, regression testing, data validation, and end-to-end testing for Workday enhancements and data loads. Review automatically available functionality delivered through Workday R1/R2 releases, assess business impact, and support regression testing. Review and disposition setup-required functionality delivered through Workday releases and coordinate appropriate configuration changes. Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to gather requirements, document solutions, and implement scalable system and data improvements. Build and maintain strong relationships with HR leaders, IT professionals, functional teams, and end users. Qualifications 4+ years of Workday functional experience, preferably supporting Workday Core HCM in a large enterprise environment. Strong hands-on experience with Workday Personal Information and Contact Information configuration and Business Processes. Demonstrated experience creating, processing, troubleshooting, and validating Workday EIBs for mass data transactions. Strong experience with HR data migration, data conversion, data mapping, cleansing, transformation, reconciliation, and validation. Experience configuring and maintaining reference letters, employment letters, document templates, and other Workday-generated documents. Strong knowledge of Workday Core HCM and the Workday Business Process Framework. Experience with Workday reporting, calculated fields, security, and Business Process Security Policies. Ability to troubleshoot complex configuration, data, EIB, and Business Process issues. Strong understanding of data integrity, data governance, and HR data management best practices. Strong written and verbal communication, analytical, documentation, and stakeholder management skills. Ability to manage multiple projects, production issues, enhancement requests, and data initiatives simultaneously. Familiarity with Workday configuration deployment and migration tools, including Tenant Compare, Configuration Change Tracker/Extracts, and Object Transporter (OX). Preferred Experience Experience supporting large-scale Workday implementations, acquisitions, reorganizations, or HR data migration/conversion projects. Exposure to Compensation, Recruiting, Absence, Benefits, and/or Payroll. Experience working in Agile or large enterprise HRIS environments. Workday certification in Core HCM and/or other relevant Workday modules. GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc). jobs.title: Claims Analyst
jobs.jd: Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam. We’re hiring a Claims Analyst to own the day-to-day integrity of our claims and adjudication workflows and to help build the processes, controls, and reporting behind them. This is a hands-on role: you’ll personally work our hardest claims and denials while standing up the playbooks, benchmarks, and dashboards that let claims operations scale without breaking. Reporting to our Manager, RCM, you’ll sit at the intersection of our clearinghouse, prior-auth, and finance systems — and you’ll be the person who can explain exactly why a claim paid, denied, or landed where it did. What you'll do: Own claims adjudication and QA. Review, validate, and adjudicate imaging claims against benefit designs, contracted rates, and our pass-through payment model; identify and resolve pricing, coding, and eligibility discrepancies before they become client or member issues. Lead denials management. Investigate root causes of denials and underpayments, drive appeals and resubmissions, and build recurring analysis that turns denial patterns into fixes upstream (prior auth, eligibility, EDI configuration). Manage EDI and clearinghouse workflows. Work hands-on in Waystar across 837P submissions, 835 remittances, and companion-guide requirements; troubleshoot rejections and payer-specific edits; partner with vendors to keep the pipes clean. Safeguard cost-share and accumulator accuracy. Ensure deductible, coinsurance, HDHP, and accumulator logic is applied correctly so members and clients are billed accurately and we stay compliant with cost-sharing rules. Own AR and aging. Monitor accounts receivable and claims aging, prioritize collectible balances, and maintain reporting that gives finance and leadership a real-time view of what’s outstanding and why. Build the reporting layer. Develop and maintain dashboards and KPIs (adjudication turnaround, denial rate, clean-claim rate, AR aging, recovery rate) from Waystar and adjacent claims data. Coordinate across the stack. Work closely with prior authorization (Infinx), finance, and client-facing teams to close the loop between authorization, exam, claim, and payment. Write the playbook. Document repeatable SOPs, edits, and escalation paths, and help train and mentor analysts as the team grows. About you: Required 2+ years in healthcare claims, revenue cycle, or medical billing, with demonstrated ownership of complex adjudication and denials work Deep hands-on experience with EDI transactions (837/835) and a clearinghouse platform (Waystar strongly preferred) Strong command of CPT/HCPCS, ICD-10, place-of-service, and modifier logic — ideally in radiology/imaging Working knowledge of benefit structures, cost-sharing, deductibles, and accumulator/HDHP mechanics Advanced spreadsheet skills and comfort building reporting from raw claims data A meticulous, audit-minded approach: you can trace any dollar to its source and defend it Preferred Experience at a TPA, benefits administrator, or payer, especially serving self-funded employers Familiarity with prior authorization workflows and tools (e.g., Infinx) Exposure to appeals, payer escalations, and underpayment recovery at scale Early-stage or high-growth environment experience — comfortable building process where none exists The salary range for this position is $50,000 - $65,000. This position is also bonus eligible. Individual compensation will depend on various factors, including qualifications, skills, experience, location, and applicable laws. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible to participate in our equity incentive and competitive benefits plans. Fraud and Security Notice: Please be aware of recent job scam attempts. Our team uses the oneimaging.com email domain exclusively. If you have been contacted by someone claiming to be a OneImaging recruiter or a hiring manager from a different domain about a potential job, please report it to law enforcement here and to candidateprotection@oneimaging.com . jobs.jd: Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Analyst, Risk Adjustment to join our Risk Adjustment team. Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family. About the role: Risk Adjustment accounts for differences in members’ health needs and expected cost of care. Accurate and complete clinical documentation helps ensure that a member’s health status is appropriately represented. Prospective Risk Adjustment focuses on proactively supporting opportunities for healthcare providers to review members’ health information and accurately document conditions addressed during clinical care, in accordance with applicable clinical coding and documentation requirements. These efforts may include sharing relevant clinical information with providers at the point of care, conducting virtual or in-home health assessments, and providing reports that identify historical or suspected conditions for provider review and clinical validation. The Analyst, Risk Adjustment supports the day-to-day execution and performance of Prospective Risk Adjustment programs. This role partners with internal teams and external vendors to ensure operational workflows are functioning as intended, program data and reporting are accurate, claims are processed appropriately, and operational issues are identified and resolved in a timely manner. The analyst will support a portfolio of initiatives including Point-of-Care tools, Virtual Health Assessments (VHA), In-Home Assessments (IHA), and provider reporting to support the review of member conditions. This role is well suited for an analytical, detail-oriented professional interested in developing expertise in Risk Adjustment and healthcare operations. You will report into the Sr. Manager, Strategic Initiatives (Risk Adjustment). Work Location: This position is based in our New York, NY office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. Thursdays are a required in-office day for team meetings and events, while your other two office days are flexible to suit your schedule. #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $75,348- $98,894 per year. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program and annual performance bonuses. Responsibilities: Prospective Risk Adjustment Program Operations (30%) – Support daily operations across prospective Risk Adjustment programs, including Point-of-Care tooling, VHA, IHA, and provider gap-reporting initiatives. Monitor program activity and workflows to ensure processes are functioning as intended; investigate operational issues and coordinate resolution or escalation as appropriate. Vendor Operations & Support (25%) – Support the day-to-day operational needs of external vendors. Coordinate recurring deliverables and data exchanges, respond to operational questions, track issues and action items, and partner with vendors and internal stakeholders to drive timely resolution. Reporting, Data Analysis & Reconciliation (20%) – Develop and maintain recurring reports, trackers, and analyses to monitor program performance, including assessment activity, provider participation, vendor performance, claims activity, and other key operational metrics. Perform data validation and reconciliation across internal and vendor data sources to identify discrepancies, trends, and opportunities for operational improvement. Point-of-Care & Provider Programs (15%) – Support programs that provide relevant member health information, including historical and suspected conditions, to healthcare providers for review and clinical validation. Support Point-of-Care tools and provider reporting initiatives and assist with resolving related data, reporting, and workflow issues. Member & Claims Operations (10%) – Support member-level program operations, including reviewing and processing appropriate exclusions from VHA and IHA programs. Monitor and reconcile claims associated with prospective Risk Adjustment initiatives to ensure appropriate processing and payment; investigate discrepancies and partner with relevant teams to support resolution. Requirements: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate operational or data-related issues and support resolution. Strong attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and recurring deliverables. Ability to work effectively with data, reporting tools, spreadsheets, and operational workflows. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams and with external partners. Bonus points Knowledge of healthcare operations, Risk Adjustment, claims, provider operations, or health plan processes. Experience analyzing data, identifying trends or discrepancies, and translating findings into actionable next steps. Proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets; familiarity with SQL, Tableau, Looker, or similar analytics tools is a plus. jobs.title: Intelligence Systems Analyst
jobs.jd:
About the Team

The Intelligence and Investigations (I2) team provides intelligence to decision makers across OpenAI and investigates severe misuse of our products. I2’s work saves lives: we disrupt real-world violence, protect children, and prevent catastrophic harms from AI misuse. We also draw on our investigations and in-depth analysis of a wide range of data sources to provide actionable quantitative and qualitative intelligence to OpenAI’s leadership.

I2 Engineering works hand in hand with I2’s analysts and investigators, building tools that expand what human experts can understand and accomplish. Our tools help them make sense of vast and complex datasets, discover and measure on-platform and off-platform risk, and investigate severe misuse with greater speed, depth, and consistency.


About the Role

We are looking for an Intelligence Systems Analyst who wants to work alongside investigators to understand difficult cases, contribute to analysis, and build tools and workflows that help the team do more. As investigators pursue leads, assess risks, and determine what happened, you’ll see where better tools could help and build them.

The role combines hands-on software and data work with meaningful participation in investigations. Depending on the problem, you might trace activity across internal systems, write a query or small application, prototype an AI-assisted workflow, improve how evidence is assembled, or turn an investigator’s recurring need into a durable product capability.

You will work closely with engineers, analysts, investigators, and other subject matter experts. Success requires enough operational understanding to contribute meaningfully to an investigation and enough technical ownership to build solutions that remain useful after the immediate case is resolved.


In this role, you will:

 - Work directly alongside investigators on complex cases, helping develop leads, analyze evidence, and identify useful technical approaches.

 - Build and maintain software, data workflows, and internal tools that accelerate investigations of potential high-severity misuse or harm.

 - Use Python, SQL, and internal data systems to gather, connect, and analyze information relevant to investigative work.

 - Apply OpenAI’s models to research, search, triage, synthesis, and evidence review in workflows that keep expert investigators informed and in control.

 - Turn recurring investigative bottlenecks into reliable tools, automation, and product capabilities that support multiple users and cases.

 - Prototype quickly when a new investigative question arises, then improve reliability, usability, and maintainability as requirements become clearer.

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

About the role

We’re looking for someone to join our Sales Strategy & Operations team and own how ElevenLabs goes to market by vertical. As we shift from a horizontal motion to a vertical-led one, you will go deep on each of our top verticals — the buyer, the use cases, the competitive landscape, and what it takes to win — and turn that into a repeatable playbook for launching and scaling each one.
