jobs.title: AI Research Resident (Algorithms Codesign)
jobs.jd:
NORMAL COMPUTING | BUILD WITH US

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.


THE RESIDENCY PROGRAM

The AI Research Residency is Normal Computing's flagship program for exceptional researchers and engineers who want to work at the frontier of AI. Residents join a small, hand-picked cohort with a dedicated research mentor, direct access to the team developing the algorithms for our in-memory inference hardware, and a clear arc from onboarding through publication.

Every residency is built around two milestones that mark you as part of something bigger than a single project: a research paper co-authored with our team, and a company-wide research colloquium where you present your findings to the full Normal Computing organization. You'll leave with a body of published, presented work, and a standing as one of the earliest residents to help define what this program becomes.


THIS TRACK: ALGORITHMS CODESIGN

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. This track is about the computational methods that make LLM inference run efficiently on it: rethinking how operations like attention, memory access, and long-context decoding should behave on hardware that computes inside memory, rather than adapting standard GPU kernels to a new chip.

You'll work on this as a co-design problem. The hardware and the algorithms are developed in parallel, so your findings feed architectural decisions rather than implementing against a fixed specification. You'll validate ideas against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.


YOUR NORMAL EXPERIENCE

This is a hands-on research residency: you'll take ownership of a real technical problem in inference algorithms for in-memory compute, work alongside the researchers and engineers building our platform, and be expected to contribute ideas, not just execute someone else's. Your job is to help turn research into production-quality research code that a team can build on. Outside-of-the-box thinking is encouraged.

You'll get direct exposure to the pace, ambiguity, and speed of decision-making that comes with working at a fast-moving, well-funded startup, where the distance between an idea on a whiteboard and a result on real hardware is measured in weeks, not years.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Develop inference algorithms for in-memory hardware. Understand which parts of LLM workloads are best suited to in-memory execution and develop algorithms that exploit it natively, demonstrated first in simulation and then on hardware.

Design numerical methods that fit the physics. Design methods that exploit thermal noise and analog dynamics rather than working around them.

Build evaluation suites and benchmarks. Help build the evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that characterize how algorithms behave on real hardware and in simulation, and tell us honestly whether any of it actually works.

Translate workloads into hardware constraints. Turn insights about model workloads into constraints and opportunities for the hardware and architecture teams.

Prototype and iterate rapidly. Move with the hardware as it evolves from simulation to FPGA to silicon.

Drive a research question of your own. Partner with researchers and engineers to scope, run, and iterate on an original technical investigation, with rigorous experimental analysis and documentation along the way.

Co-author a paper. Work with the team to write up your findings for submission to a relevant venue, with mentorship on framing, experiments, and technical writing. One of the two milestones every resident builds toward.

Present at the residency colloquium. Share your work and thinking with the broader Normal Computing research community at the program's capstone event, and get real-time feedback from people building this technology every day.


WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU A GREAT FIT

Currently pursuing or recently completed a graduate degree (MS or PhD, or equivalent research experience) in machine learning, applied mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field. Publications are a strong plus, but not required at the resident level; a solid research track record is what matters.

A working understanding of large model inference: attention mechanisms, KV cache, long-context decoding, memory bandwidth constraints. Deep production experience isn't expected at the resident level, but the intuition should feel familiar.

Some exposure to inference optimization (quantization, sparsity, kernel fusion, or memory-efficient attention), or to stochastic systems, probabilistic methods, numerical analysis, or analog computation.

Strong Python skills, plus some experience with a systems language (C++, Rust, or similar) or with implementing algorithms close to hardware, beyond high-level frameworks.

Some experience (course projects, research, or otherwise) turning a research idea into working, reasonably reproducible code. You care about whether results replicate, not just whether a demo works once.

Comfort reasoning from first principles about what a novel substrate can do efficiently.

Bonus: exposure to analog or mixed-signal systems, in-memory compute, or non-von-Neumann architectures; publications or open-source work in efficient inference, stochastic algorithms, or novel computing; or experience working on hardware that did not yet exist when you joined.

Strong written and verbal communication skills; prior experience writing up research (papers, theses, technical reports) is a plus, as is any experience presenting technical work to a live audience.

A bias toward ownership and self-direction. You're energized, not overwhelmed, by the ambiguity and speed of a small, fast-moving startup.

jobs.title: Real Estate Market Intelligence Analyst
jobs.jd:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

Neko is opening clinics at pace: from a handful of US sites today to a 2028 cohort in the dozens and a portfolio in the hundreds by 2030. We are looking for a flexible, quantitative analyst to build the market intelligence behind that growth, using GIS, data, and analytics to decide where we open next, why, and how many clinics a market can support. The work runs from market sizing and member analytics through to site, market, and portfolio performance.

This is a build role. Neko is appointment-based, not footfall-driven, so the standard retail playbook does not transfer, and working out what predicts a successful clinic is the core problem. There is no framework to inherit: you will build the models and processes from scratch, and what you build in year one is what the whole portfolio runs on.

You will report to the Head of US Real Estate and work closely with the Transaction Managers, the Real Estate Associates, and our data analytics and engineering teams, in a small team where you help set the standard.




WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6-12 MONTHS

 - Market sizing: size the addressable member base by market and trade area, and translate it into how many clinics a market can support and in what order we should enter. This is the first priority of the role.

 - Site selection support: give Real Estate the analysis to justify new markets and infill locations, and to decide clinic sizing and spacing, including overlap and cannibalization as density increases.

 - Member data foundation: work with the internal data analytics and engineering teams to set up the full chain, from data collection to aggregation to analysis. Define our ideal member profile, find where those members live and work, and keep refining it as first-party data accumulates.

 - GIS platform, tool agnostic: use GrowthFactor today and own the catchment definitions, data layers, and scoring logic. Document the logic independently of the tool so it moves with us, and help evaluate and onboard the next platform when the time comes. Make the tool usable by Transaction Managers, not only by you.

 - Scoring and forecasting models: maintain a repeatable, defensible site scoring model and demand forecasts built to be re-run. A reforecast after a slipped opening or a shifted plan should be a scenario switch, not a rebuild.

 - Portfolio, market, and site performance: as clinics open, track and review performance at the portfolio, market, and site level. Compare forecast to actual, separate a bad site from a bad market from a bad launch, surface underperformers early, and document what each opening teaches us. Turn those learnings into updated site selection criteria, scoring weights, and sizing and spacing rules, so every new clinic is chosen with better information than the last.

 - Approval memos and cross-functional support: help produce LOI and Lease Approval Memos by coordinating inputs from Real Estate, Design, Construction, and Legal into a clear, one-page recommendation that leadership can decide from.

 - Process design and redesign: own the evaluation processes the team runs on, and version them. Retire what stops working, rebuild what needs it, and write it down so others can run it without you.

 - AI across the Real Estate team: use Claude and custom agents to eliminate your own manual work, then go further. Identify where AI can save broader team time (market research, data pulls, memo drafting, lease and LOI summaries, pipeline reporting), build reusable prompts, skills, and agents, train teammates to use them, and track the time saved. Be honest about where AI output needs human review.

 - Market packs and benchmarks: produce market entry recommendations, ranked pipeline views, and site-level briefs, backed by per-site cost and occupancy benchmarks by market so deal comparison sits on real data.
   
   


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3 to 6 years in real estate market analytics, site selection, location intelligence, data science, or strategy, ideally supporting multi-site physical expansion.

 - Hands-on GIS experience with GrowthFactor, Esri ArcGIS, Kalibrate, Buxton, SiteZeus, Placer, or similar. We care more that you understand catchment and scoring logic than that you know any one tool, because the tool will change.

 - Strong market sizing and quantitative skills: penetration and capture modeling, regression or other predictive approaches, and scenario and sensitivity analysis. Excel to a high standard.

 - Comfort with census, consumer spend, mobility, and first-party data, and honesty about the limits of each.

 - Financial literacy: you can build a basic site pro forma, calculate payback and break-even, and connect a demand forecast to a real estate decision.

 - Flexibility. You can tear down your own model without ego, rebuild it when the facts change, and stay organized while priorities shift.

 - Clear communication and intellectual honesty. You can defend an assumption to a skeptical executive in two minutes, name the two things most likely to be wrong, and say early when the data does not support the answer people want.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - SQL or Python, which helps you work alongside engineers.

 - Specific, demonstrable use of AI to speed up analytical work, and real interest in teaching others to do the same.

 - Exposure to healthcare or regulated markets, or to European or multi-region expansion.

jobs.title: Pricing Strategy Analyst (Remote)
jobs.jd: We're looking for a Pricing Strategy Analyst to join Procore's Corporate Strategy team. In this role, you'll be the data and analytics engine behind our pricing, packaging, and monetization strategy, turning transaction, sales, and product data into the commercial signals that inform our decisions. You'll also lead smaller pricing initiatives across the full Procore portfolio, including our emerging AI offerings. The primary goal of this role is to make sure Procore's pricing decisions are grounded in clear, accurate, and well-sourced data. As a Pricing Strategy Analyst , you'll partner with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing to analyze how our pricing and packaging perform in the market and to build the visibility needed to improve them. Use your structured problem-solving, data analysis, and executive communication skills to shape how Procore captures value from what we build and buy. If you want hands-on work to drive top line growth and connect everyone in construction, apply today and join our team! This position reports to the Senior Manager of Pricing & Monetization Strategy and can be based remotely in the US. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: Lead pricing and packaging initiatives from hypothesis through recommendation, in partnership with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing Build and stress-test the business case behind pricing decisions, including segment-level performance, cannibalization-adjusted ARR impact, and migration and monetization sizing. Analyze transaction, bookings, discounting, and product data to identify the commercial signals that explain how our pricing and packaging perform, and diagnose the root cause when they underperform, whether it is package design, sales execution, or market fit. Design and run market, competitive, and willingness-to-pay research, including win/loss and price elasticity analysis, to pressure-test pricing hypotheses before they reach leadership. Build and maintain pricing and packaging reporting and dashboards that give Product, Sales, and Finance visibility into performance, working with data teams to keep metrics and data sources accurate and consistent. Translate analysis into a small number of clear, claim-driven recommendations, present them to executive leaders, and defend them under challenge. Partner with Pricing Operations, Sales, Customer Success, Deal Desk, and Marketing to make sure approved decisions are operationalized and communicated to the field. What we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or a related field. 3+ years of experience in pricing, monetization, strategy, business or data analytics, financial planning and analysis, or consulting wi th 2+ y ears inside a pricing or monetization practice at a top-tier strategy firm Track record of framing ambiguous problems into clear analytical frameworks and presenting recommendations to cross-functional and senior audiences. Experience leading projects or workstreams from analysis through recommendation, with the ability to balance multiple priorities. Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills, with experience building revenue impact and unit economics models. Hands-on experience querying and analyzing large datasets (e.g., SQL), building reports in a BI tool (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) is a plus Ability to synthesize qualitative inputs, such as call transcripts and field feedback, into clear themes that support pricing recommendations. Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills, with experience partnering with Product, Sales, Finance, and Marketing teams. Familiarity with B2B SaaS metrics (e.g., ARR, net revenue retention, win rate, discount rate) is a plus Curiosity, high agency, and an owner’s mindset with a strong bias for action. Additional Information Base Pay Range: 81,600.00 - 112,200.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

jobs.jd: Convene Hospitality Group (CHG) operates a global portfolio of lifestyle brands focused on creating places and experiences that bring people together. The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well. If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team. Analytics Engineer We’re hiring Analytics Engineers to join Convene Hospitality Group’s (CHG) Technology organization. We’re building out the foundational platform to democratize data at CHG so that a venue GM, a finance lead, and an AI agent are all able to ask a question and get the same trusted answer. Analytics engineers own the full path from ingestion to visualization, including governance and observability. You’ll bring data in from source systems, model it through bronze, silver, and gold, define the semantic layer, and breathe life into the visualizations, conversational analytics, and business agents that teams rely on to make decisions. You’ll join the Data Platform team, reporting to its Engineering Manager, and work closely with other analytics engineers and business partners across the company. You’ll build on Snowflake, dbt, and Fivetran, using Snowflake-native capabilities like semantic views and Cortex to power ThoughtSpot and beyond. What You’ll Do: Partner with the business. Work with Finance, Sales, Operations, and venue teams to understand their needs and turn them into models and metrics they trust. Own ingestion for your domains. Set up and maintain Fivetran connectors, land data in bronze, and handle schema drift and load failures. Model the business. Build dbt models that move data through bronze, silver, and gold, and shape gold around how CHG runs so people outside the data team can understand and use it. Own the semantic layer. Set metrics, dimensions, and relationships so a number means the same thing in a dashboard, a search, or an agent’s answer. Tune synonyms and descriptions so a model picks the right measure, trace wrong answers to the root cause, and help us decide where each definition lives. Power self-service in ThoughtSpot. Build the models and Liveboards that let teams explore data on their own, and turn the questions people actually ask into new test cases. Own the quality of conversational analytics. Test answers the way you’d test code. Build and maintain a golden question set of real business questions paired with certified answers as your test cases, run them as a regression suite on every model or semantic change, and block releases that fail. Back your models with dbt tests and clear documentation. Apply governance day to day. Tag sensitive data at ingestion, apply access controls such as tag-based masking and row access policies, and follow the standards the team sets, so an agent only returns what the person asking is allowed to see. Keep it fast and fresh. Monitor freshness, data quality, and pipeline health so problems surface to you before they reach a dashboard or an agent’s answer. Tune query and model performance, from incremental dbt models to warehouse sizing, so answers come back fast and Snowflake costs stay in check. Work AI-native. Lead with specs, then hand agents end-to-end tasks, from exploring source data to building models, tests, and documentation. Let agents run loose in the wild (with some guardrails in place). You hold agent and human work to the same review bar, so code from Claude and code from a teammate get the same scrutiny. Share what you learn, and help set the playbook for agentic data work. What We Look For: You have 3+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI development, building data products people rely on. You write strong SQL and have built and maintained dbt models in production. You’ve worked in a cloud data warehouse, ideally Snowflake. You’ve worked with ELT ingestion tools like Fivetran and can troubleshoot source-data issues such as schema changes, late-arriving data, and API limits. You understand data modeling: dimensional models, medallion layering, and clear reasoning about grain, slowly changing dimensions, and event lifecycles. You’ve built dashboards or self-service data products that people use to make decisions. You test and document your work as a habit. You’re curious about the business. You ask what decision a request supports before you start building. You use AI agents for real multi-step work, like writing SQL and dbt models, generating tests, and drafting documentation, and you verify what they produce. You explain your work clearly to technical and non-technical partners. You take ownership. You see work through, ask for help when you’re stuck, and look for ways to make things better. Bonus Points You’ve evaluated LLM or natural-language analytics output, for example with golden sets or regression testing. You’ve worked in hospitality, events, real estate, or another customer-centric, multi-location business. jobs.jd: (ID: 2026-3889) Axle is a bioscience and information technology company that offers advancements in translational research, biomedical informatics, and data science applications to research centers and healthcare organizations nationally and abroad. With experts in biomedical science, software engineering, and program management, we focus on developing and applying research tools and techniques to empower decision-making and accelerate research discoveries. We work with some of the top research organizations and facilities in the country including multiple institutes at the National Institutes of Health (NIH). The incumbent will characterize organoid fidelity, identify biomarkers of successful differentiation, and develop computational frameworks for organoid quality assessment, while gaining substantive training in integrative analysis of single-cell and multi-omics data. Pipeline development. Develop and implement computational pipelines for data processing, quality control, and statistical analysis, and document them so that analyses are reproducible across the Center. Benchmarking. Integrate SOM-generated data with publicly available datasets in order to benchmark organoid characteristics against normal tissue profiles. Method development. Develop and refine analytical approaches — including machine learning methods where appropriate — for classifying cellular states and assessing organoid quality, and contribute to standardized assessment protocols. Collaboration and interpretation. Work closely with experimental teams to interpret results and guide protocol optimization, and collaborate with other computational staff on cross-modality data integration. Dissemination. Contribute to manuscript preparation and present findings at scientific conferences. Required Qualifications Education. Doctoral degree (PhD) in bioinformatics, computational biology, biostatistics, or a related quantitative field, completed or anticipated prior to the start of the appointment. Single-cell analysis. Extensive experience with single-cell data analysis, including familiarity with tools such as Seurat, Scanpy, or comparable platforms. Programming. Strong programming proficiency in R and Python, together with experience in statistical analysis and data visualization. Omics workflows. Working knowledge of proteomics and metabolomics data analysis workflows. Preferred Qualifications Prior experience analyzing organoid datasets. Experience with machine learning approaches for biological data, familiarity with pathway analysis tools, and knowledge of developmental biology principles. Experience with high-performance computing environments and version control systems. jobs.title: Public Sector Delivery Analyst
jobs.jd:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


ROLE OVERVIEW:

We're growing our Canadian Public Sector Delivery team and hiring Public Sector Delivery Analysts to help run some of the most consequential AI deployments in the country. You'll work alongside our Engineering Program Managers (EPMs), Technical Leads, and senior leadership to keep large, multi-stakeholder government programs organized, documented, and moving.

This is a hands-on delivery role for individuals who want exposure to enterprise AI and high-stakes program delivery while taking pride in making complex programs run smoothly. As a member of our small, senior team, you'll deliver sovereign AI to the Government of Canada, engage directly with clients from day one on a clear path toward leading engagements, and learn how frontier AI products are deployed in real, high-security environments.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Drive things to closure. Partner with the EPM and Technical Leads to track actions, dependencies, and blockers across Cohere and client teams making sure nothing slips.

 - Show up in front of the client. Prepare and coordinate client sessions, capture outcomes, and progressively lead working-level sessions such as use-case and story refinement.

 - Run the cadence. Own the meeting and reporting rhythm including agendas, scheduling, minutes, and follow-ups so every forum lands on time with clear next steps.

 - Own the delivery artefacts. Build and maintain the plans, status reports, RAID logs, decision records, use-case registers, and traceability documentation that keep our engagements audit-ready and our clients confident.

 - Keep the record straight. Maintain a single source of truth for program documentation in our public sector document management environment.
   


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 1–4 years of experience in technology or management consulting, professional services, or an in-house technical delivery team.

 - Delivery discipline. You've run RAID, action, and decision logs, refined user stories, maintained project plans on real projects and kept them accurate and clear.

 - Client presence. You can lead a working session in front of a client, read the room, and know what to say and what to hold.

 - Strong written communication. You think through the message before you build the slide. Advanced PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.

 - Technical fluency. You're comfortable discussing APIs, integrations, environments, testing, and releases. You can talk with engineers and report back accurately.

 - Follow-through. You close items without a second reminder and know what to escalate and when.

 - Eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance.

 - Based in the Ottawa area.

 - University Degree in Business/Commerce, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering or similar preferred.

 - Nice-to-have: High degree of French language proficiency.
   


WORKING LOCATION:

This role is hybrid with the requirement to be based out of Ottawa - note, there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement.

This role requires eligibility for a Government of Canada security clearance and a high degree of French language proficiency is a nice-to-have.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

jobs.title: LN Concerts, Social Insights Analyst
jobs.jd: Job Summary: WHO ARE WE? Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide. Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com . WHO ARE YOU? Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on! THE JOB The Social Insights Analyst will play a key role in Live Nation Entertainment’s Concert division, living and breathing in social listening, reporting and analytics from start to finish, including query building, dashboard development and delivering reports. This role will uncover insights and trends for actionable storytelling opportunities, guide marketing strategy, and inform cross-functional partners on social, cultural, and influencer trends. Reporting to the Sr. Manager, Analytics & Strategy, this position is ideal for someone who thrives in building scalable analytics systems while staying deeply connected to cultural and platform trends and developments. We're looking for a data-minded storyteller who lives at the intersection of social media and analytics. You'll own reporting and measurement for earned conversation tied to tours, on-sales, and artist activations. This is a great fit for someone who's equally comfortable in a spreadsheet and a comment section. WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO Own measurement and analysis of earned social conversation: mentions, share of voice, sentiment, engagement on non-owned posts, organic reach, and virality across Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, and emerging platforms. Run social listening across tour cycles (from announcements, on-sales to live moments), tracking fan sentiment, conversation volume, and flagging shifts in real time. Measure fan- and creator-generated content (UGC): what's made, how it spreads, which moments drive organic amplification, and how artists, media, and fan accounts pick it up. Build and maintain dashboards and recurring reports (daily, weekly, campaign-level, ad-hoc, and post-mortem), using Boolean logic to sharpen queries and insights delivery. Run competitive and benchmark analysis to contextualize our performance. Build alert systems for emerging artist topics, trends, and brand risks, supporting Community Management, Marketing, and PR/Comms in shaping response messaging. Partner with social listening-tool vendors and cross-functional teams to improve benchmarks, KPIs, alerts, and depth of insight. Uncover fan insights through audience demographics to help guide campaign planning WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING 2–4 years in social media analytics, social listening, and/or digital insights with a focus on earned measurement (agency or in-house social team preferred). Hands-on experience with social listening and publishing tools (Meltwater, Brandwatch, Sprout, Quid, etc.) plus platform-native analytics. Comfortable with audience demographic tools such as Audiense as well as platform follower demographics through CreatorIQ. Fluency in earned-social metrics (share of voice, sentiment, mention volume) and a clear sense of which ones actually matter. Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills and a solid grasp of Boolean logic for query development. Proven ability to own analytics end-to-end (query design, reporting, dashboard development and maintenance), with a track record of spotting and fixing gaps in reporting infrastructure. Deep understanding of social platforms as both a fan and an analyst: how conversation forms, why things spread, what fans respond to, plus genuine curiosity about cultural trends, emerging formats, and creator marketing. Strong communication skills: you can turn a spike in conversation into a one-slide "so what" for non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented, organized, and able to juggle multiple projects and deadlines under pressure. A proactive, collaborative team player who flags insights before they're asked for and adapts to evolving leadership needs. Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Analytics, or a related field. NICE TO HAVE: Passion for live music, touring, and artist marketing. Experience with sentiment analysis, text/topic classification, or unstructured conversation data. Familiarity with creator/influencer earned-coverage measurement. Experience connecting earned social signals to broader marketing or fan-growth outcomes. BENEFITS & PERKS Our motto is ‘Taking Care of Our Own’ through 6 pillars of benefits: HEALTH : Medical, vision, dental and mental health benefits for you and your family, with access to a health care concierge, and Flexible or Health Savings Accounts (FSA or HSA) YOURSELF : Free concert tickets, generous paid time off including paid holidays, sick time, and personal days WEALTH : 401(k) program with company match, stock reimbursement program FAMILY : New parent programs including caregiver leave, plus fertility, adoption, foster, or surrogacy support CAREER : Career and skill development programs with School of Live, tuition reimbursement, and student loan repayment OTHERS : Volunteer time off, crowdfunding match EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY We aspire to build teams that reflect and support the fans and artists we serve. Every day we aim to promote environments where everyone can be themselves, contribute fully, and thrive within our company and at our events. jobs.jd:
About Gen

Gen is a global company dedicated to powering Digital Freedom through its trusted consumer brands including Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion and more. Our combined heritage is rooted in financial empowerment and cyber safety for the first digital generations, and today we deliver award-winning cybersecurity, online privacy, identity protection and financial wellness solutions to nearly 500 million users in more than 150 countries.  

Together, we share a collective passion and vision to protect consumers and help them grow, manage and secure their digital and financial lives. We’re always looking for smart, fearless and high-impact talent who see AI as a teammate – leveraging it to move faster and deliver meaningful results.  

When you’re part of Gen, you’ll have the flexibility, tools and support to do your best work and grow your career – from flexible working options and time off to competitive pay, benefits and well-being programs.  

At Gen, we are scrappy and relentlessly customer driven. We create room for healthy debate, experimentation and continuous learning, and we seek out people with different experiences, identities and ideas to join our team. You’ll work with people who back each other, respect each other and understand that our differences are a competitive advantage.  

If this sounds like you, we’d love you to be part of Gen. 

 

About the Role

We are looking for a Data Scientist to develop data solutions that will enable us to assist critical day to day business decisions.

As a Data Scientist in the Decision Science role, you will have the opportunity to apply analytics, experimentation and machine learning algorithms to support and enhance MoneyLion’s products with data driven decisions.

You will be embedded within the product teams and deliver tangible business value by deploying or refining solutions ranging from fraud and credit underwriting to user experience optimisations, providing convincing evidence of their effectiveness. This entails designing, developing, validating, deploying and monitoring the outcome of experiments using (and refining) business objectives that will ultimately increase revenue and reduce business costs. You will partner with Product, Data Engineers and Machine Learning teams, exploring and utilizing the frontier of innovation, in order to augment analytics with AI, rapidly iterate with configurable experiments, monitor and evaluate key developments, and understand business needs intimately to help develop valuable AI solutions.

 

About MoneyLion

MoneyLion is a leader in financial technology powering the next generation of personalized products and content, with a top consumer finance super app, a premier embedded finance platform for enterprise businesses and a world-class media arm. MoneyLion’s mission is to give everyone the power to make their best financial decisions. We pride ourselves on serving the many, not the few; providing confidence through guidance, choice, personalization; and shortening the distance to an informed action.

In our go-to money app for consumers, we deliver curated content on finance and related topics, through a tailored feed that engages people to learn and share. People take control of their finances with our innovative financial products and marketplace - including our full-fledged suite of features to save, borrow, spend, and invest - seamlessly bringing together the best offers and content from MoneyLion and our 1,100+ Enterprise Partner network, together in one experience. MoneyLion’s enterprise technology provides the definitive search engine and marketplace for financial products, enabling any company to add embedded finance to their business, with advanced AI-backed data and tools through our platform and API. Established in 2013, MoneyLion connects millions of people with the financial products and content they need, when and where they need it.

 

Key Responsibilities

 - Perform analyses to understand how our users interact with our products and how to improve our products

 - Communicate findings to stakeholders in a clear and concise manner

 - Identify anomalies and investigate the root causes of anomalies

 - Design and build experiments to solve challenging data and business problems

 - Collaborate with product owners to discover new insights and understanding of business performance based on data

 - Identify trends and opportunities from the data and influence product roadmaps

 - Develop dashboards to track relevant metrics

 - Recommend ways to measure success

 - Work with engineers to improve the data collection process

 - Ensure data-driven decision making within the organization

 - Apply, develop or refine AI algorithms to deliver business value

 

About You

 - Strong mathematical, statistical or actuarial background

 - Must have hands on experience in machine learning, predictive analytics and statistical modeling

 - Proficiency with A/B testing and experimentation framework is preferred

 - Adept at problem solving using both textbook methods and novel viewpoints

 - Proficient in programming languages such as Python and SQL

 - Knowledge of data structures, data modeling, software architecture and machine learning algorithms will be an advantage

 - Demonstrably experienced with data visualization

 - Demonstrably excellent verbal and written communication skills

 

What's Next... 

After you submit your application, you can expect the following steps in the recruitment process:

 - Online Technical Test

 - Take-Home Assessment

 - Interview & Discussion of Take-Home Assessment - Hiring Manager (Virtual or face-to-face)

 - Bar Raiser Interview (Where Needed)


Gen is an equal opportunity employer, and we’re committed to fair, inclusive practices at every stage of the candidate and employee journey. Employment decisions are based on merit, experience and business needs.

jobs.title: Market Analyst
jobs.jd:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns a fleet of distributed batteries and the households we serve into a power business that makes money. As a Market Analyst, you’ll know how much Base is earning, where it could lose money, and how it will make money in the next market.

You’ll own P&L (profit and loss) reporting and risk tracking across our battery fleet and retail operations. You’ll build the pricing models behind what we charge members, recommend hedges, and work with Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy to figure out how Base makes money in each new market. Base already does this in ERCOT. Your first job is to do it in PJM.

This role suits someone with a few years of experience in power markets, retail energy, or a related analytical field. You’ll own real decisions early.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build a bottoms-up retail pricing model for PJM that builds upon our ERCOT model.

 - Bring PJM into our risk system and P&L reporting, so we know the margin we earn and how to buy supply.

 - Identify new market opportunities and work closely with stakeholders from Finance, Growth and Legal & Policy teams to bring them to reality.

 - Recommend changes to Base’s hedging strategy in ERCOT and PJM, and track our exposure against risk limits.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Energy markets knowledge: you understand wholesale market basics in ERCOT and PJM, including how power is bought, hedged and settled. You know how retail pricing and operations work.

 - Commercial sense: you understand how a retail offer makes or loses money. You can explain the cost to supply it, the margin on it, and the risk in between.

 - Risk and statistics: you think in distributions, not point forecasts. You know power prices are tail heavy. Basic statistics is enough.

 - Coding and SQL: you build reports and models in Python (or another language), pull your own data with SQL, and work through a problem independently.

Nice to have: experience at a retail energy provider, utility supply desk, or trading middle office.



ABOUT THE TEAM

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns the grid-service capability of our distributed battery fleet into revenue. That means building and defending the models that decide which markets and products Base participates in, from real-time arbitrage to multi-year distribution deals. The team’s calls carry real weight - a mis-modeled coincident peak or an unvetted market opinion shows up directly in Base’s book. You’ll work alongside traders, market operations engineers, and policy leads who bring the same rigor to distribution-scale energy that a trading desk brings to wholesale power.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

ABOUT GEN:

Gen is a global company dedicated to powering Digital Freedom through its trusted consumer brands including Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion and more. Our combined heritage is rooted in financial empowerment and cyber safety for the first digital generations, and today we deliver award-winning cybersecurity, online privacy, identity protection and financial wellness solutions to nearly 500 million users in more than 150 countries.

Together, we share a collective passion and vision to protect consumers and help them grow, manage and secure their digital and financial lives. We’re always looking for smart, fearless and high-impact talent who see AI as a teammate – leveraging it to move faster and deliver meaningful results.

When you’re part of Gen, you’ll have the flexibility, tools and support to do your best work and grow your career – from flexible working options and time off to competitive pay, benefits and well-being programs.

At Gen, we are scrappy and relentlessly customer driven. We create room for healthy debate, experimentation and continuous learning, and we seek out people with different experiences, identities and ideas to join our team. You’ll work with people who back each other, respect each other and understand that our differences are a competitive advantage.

If this sounds like you, we’d love you to be part of Gen.




ROLE OVERVIEW

The Marketing Analyst – Network Optimization will use data and experimentation to uncover what drives marketplace performance, turning analysis into clear, actionable recommendations that shape the strategy, execution, and continuous improvement of tests. Key Responsibilities

Marketplace and Marketing Analytics

 - Partner with analytics and data science teams to improve measurement quality, data reliability, and experimentation velocity.

 - Identify meaningful changes, anomalies, and emerging opportunities that require investigation or follow-up testing.

 - Maintain consistent standards for experiment documentation, naming, tracking, and knowledge sharing.

 - Capture and distribute learnings so that successful approaches can be scaled and unsuccessful approaches can inform future tests.

Required Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in marketing analytics, statistics, economics, business, mathematics, computer science, or a related quantitative field.

 - 1–3 years of experience in marketing analytics, product analytics, growth analytics, experimentation, revenue analytics, or a related discipline.

 - Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous, and cross-functional environment.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Exposure to funnel analysis, offer ranking, pricing, partner optimization, customer segmentation, or revenue optimization.

 - Experience coordinating cross-functional projects or maintaining a structured test backlog.

 - Experience presenting analytical findings and recommendations to business stakeholders.

What Success Looks Like

 - Tests are well documented, launched on schedule, and aligned to clearly defined business questions.

 - Stakeholders have an accurate, up-to-date view of the test agenda, status, owners, dependencies, and next steps.

 - Test readouts are timely, accurate, and easy to understand.

 - Reporting helps teams identify performance changes, prioritize opportunities, and make faster decisions.

 - Takes ownership, follows through, and proactively communicates risks or blockers.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Mail
jobs.jd:
For this role on the Mail team, Superhuman offers a remote-flexible work model, whereas other Data Science roles may be aligned with a specific hub based on business needs. This gives team members plenty of focus time and the flexibility to do their best work wherever they're based, while staying closely connected to a collaborative, tight-knit team culture. A hybrid setup is available for those based in San Francisco, New York City, or Seattle.




ABOUT SUPERHUMAN

Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. The Superhuman suite of apps and agents brings AI wherever people work, integrating with over 1 million applications and websites. The company's products include Grammarly's writing assistance, Docs’ collaborative workspace, Mail's inbox management, and Go, the proactive AI assistant that understands context and automatically delivers help. Founded in 2009, Superhuman empowers over 40 million people, 50,000 organizations, and 3,000 educational institutions worldwide to eliminate busywork and focus on what matters. Learn more at superhuman.com http://superhuman.com and about our values here https://superhuman.com/company/values.




THE OPPORTUNITY

Want to use data science to shape how one of the most beloved productivity products in the world grows, retains, and delights its users? This Data Scientist position is embedded in the Superhuman Mail https://superhuman.com/mail business unit, working alongside Data Engineering, Finance, RevOps, and UX Market Research. Together, you act as one numbers-and-insights team, with a direct line to the leaders setting strategy and a shared mandate to move the metrics that matter.



Superhuman Mail is the fastest, most AI-native email experience ever built. It helps knowledge workers and teams fly through their inbox twice as fast, stay on top of what matters most, and collaborate without friction — saving users four hours every single week. Where email has barely changed in decades, Superhuman Mail is reimagining it from the ground up: AI that drafts replies in your voice, auto-labels and triages incoming messages, surfaces follow-ups before you drop the ball, and can even send emails on your behalf. It serves everyone, from individual professionals to Fortune 500 sales teams, and boasts a deeply loyal user base and a product people genuinely love. The data environment is rich, the growth questions are hard, and the opportunity to drive real impact — on acquisition, activation, retention, and expansion — is enormous.



Your work on Mail is part of a broader platform story. The Superhuman Platform suite includes Grammarly's writing assistance, Mail, Docs, Databases, and Go, our proactive AI assistant. As a compound startup, we're building an integrated suite rather than separate tools — so insights you surface in Mail ripple across the full product portfolio, and cross-product growth loops connect the dots between how users discover, adopt, and expand across the suite. Our products serve both consumers and enterprises, creating an unusually rich data environment. Our user base spans students and knowledge workers, individual users and Fortune 500 companies, universities and global enterprises, across a growing range of languages and markets. That breadth creates no shortage of important questions to own.



This is an opportunity for those drawn to complex, high-stakes growth problems — in a product people are passionate about — who want their work to measurably change outcomes.



What you’ll do

 - Be the embedded data science partner for the Mail core product team — shaping feature strategy, prioritization, and roadmap decisions with evidence, not just fielding ad hoc requests.

 - Define and own the metrics that matter for Mail: activation milestones, engagement depth, retention curves, and the leading indicators that tell us whether a new feature is actually changing how people work in their inbox.

 - Design and run experiments across the Mail product lifecycle — from onboarding and first-week activation to long-term habit formation — and build the measurement frameworks that separate signal from noise.

 - Shape the measurement strategy for Mail's AI features — Auto Drafts, Auto Labels, Auto Archive, Calendar, MCP, and the agentic capabilities on the roadmap — by defining quality frameworks and behavioral metrics that show whether AI is making users genuinely faster and more effective.

 - Figure out what makes Mail sticky: which features drive the deepest engagement, what the activation sequence looks like for users who become power users, and where in the funnel we're leaving value on the table.

 - Partner with product-led and sales-led growth to identify and quantify the levers that turn individual users into team expansions — and surface the product signals that predict conversion and churn.

 - Use data to craft remarkable product moments — turning behavioral insight into smarter onboarding flows, better feature discovery, and engagement nudges that feel natural rather than forced. jobs.title: Product Data Scientist - Youth, Families and Learning
jobs.jd:
About the role

We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

 - Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

 - Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.

 - Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.

 - Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.

 - Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results.

 - Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently.

 - Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.

 - The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

 - Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.

 - Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work.

Helpful experience

Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time.

jobs.jd:
About Gen
Gen is a global company dedicated to powering Digital Freedom through its trusted consumer brands including Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion and more. Our combined heritage is rooted in financial empowerment and cyber safety for the first digital generations, and today we deliver award-winning cybersecurity, online privacy, identity protection and financial wellness solutions to nearly 500 million users in more than 150 countries.

Together, we share a collective passion and vision to protect consumers and help them grow, manage and secure their digital and financial lives. We’re always looking for smart, fearless and high-impact talent who see AI as a teammate – leveraging it to move faster and deliver meaningful results.

When you’re part of Gen, you’ll have the flexibility, tools and support to do your best work and grow your career – from flexible working options and time off to competitive pay, benefits and well-being programs.

We create room for healthy debate, experimentation and continuous learning, and we seek out people with different experiences, identities and ideas to join our team. You’ll work with people who back each other, respect each other and understand that our differences are a competitive advantage.

If this sounds like you, we’d love you to be part of Gen.

 

About MoneyLion

MoneyLion is a leader in financial technology powering the next generation of personalized products and content, with a top consumer finance super app, a premier embedded finance platform for enterprise businesses and a world-class media arm. MoneyLion’s mission is to give everyone the power to make their best financial decisions. We pride ourselves on serving the many, not the few; providing confidence through guidance, choice, personalization; and shortening the distance to an informed action.

 

In our go-to money app for consumers, we deliver curated content on finance and related topics, through a tailored feed that engages people to learn and share. People take control of their finances with our innovative financial products and marketplace - including our full-fledged suite of features to save, borrow, spend, and invest - seamlessly bringing together the best offers and content from MoneyLion and our 1,100+ Enterprise Partner network, together in one experience. MoneyLion’s enterprise technology provides the definitive search engine and marketplace for financial products, enabling any company to add embedded finance to their business, with advanced AI-backed data and tools through our platform and API. Established in 2013, MoneyLion connects millions of people with the financial products and content they need, when and where they need it.

 

About the Role

We are looking for an Applied AI Scientist (Generative AI) who is passionate about exploring and applying the latest advances in AI to create impactful products, capabilities, and experiences.

This is a hands-on role that combines experimentation, application development, and technical innovation. You will work with frontier AI technologies, explore emerging techniques, and transform promising ideas into practical AI-powered solutions.

The ideal candidate is curious, adaptable, and excited by the rapidly evolving AI landscape. You enjoy building, learning, and experimenting with new technologies while maintaining a strong focus on delivering meaningful outcomes.

 

Key Responsibilities

 - Explore emerging Generative AI technologies, models, frameworks, and tools, and apply relevant innovations to practical AI-powered solutions.

 - Design and develop applications, workflows, agents, and intelligent systems.

 - Build and evolve AI-powered solutions from concept to production.

 - Improve the quality, reliability, and effectiveness of AI-powered solutions through testing, iteration, and continuous improvement.

 - Collaborate with scientists, engineers, and product teams to develop and deliver AI-powered capabilities.

 - Help build reliable, high-quality, and responsible AI solutions.

 

About You

 - Passionate about Generative AI and emerging AI technologies.

 - Hands-on experience building applications using modern AI models, platforms, and tools.

 - Familiarity with modern Generative AI concepts such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic workflows, tool use, model evaluation, or AI orchestration patterns.

 - Strong technical judgment, software development, and problem-solving skills.

 - Able to independently drive projects from idea to implementation.

 - Curious, adaptable, and committed to continuous learning.

 - Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively with diverse teams.
   
   

Nice to Have

 - Experience developing AI-powered products or capabilities in production environments.

 - Experience with machine learning, data science, experimentation, or other analytical techniques.

 - Experience contributing to open-source projects, technical communities, hackathons, research initiatives, or personal AI projects.

 - Experience working with large-scale data, analytics, or complex systems.

 

What’s Next

 - Take-Home Assessment

 - Hiring Manager Interview

jobs.title: Mercor AI Research Fund Grants: Economics of AI
jobs.jd:
ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.


MERCOR AI RESEARCH FUND GRANTS: ECONOMICS OF AI

One of the biggest challenges facing the industry today is determining whether frontier AI is capable enough to deliver value in real-world settings. A model can perform well on benchmarks and still struggle in production. That’s why investing in research, realistic evaluations, and robust verification is critical.

Mercor is seeking to fund AI research on the economic impacts of AI. This is separate from the Mercor Research Fellowship, which funds individual experts (apply HERE https://www.mercor.com/careers/a0a98be0-d856-4129-b500-c0a3e412ef01/), our $5m of safety funding awards (apply HERE https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/mercor/1d59ce50-4207-4d95-b7fd-5a01e90b0897), and our funding of benchmarking research.

The grant supports:

 - The time of experts from Mercor's platform

 - Researcher hours

 - API costs

 - Stipends for event and conference attendance


BUDGET CATEGORIES

Applications are grouped into three budget tiers. Please state your tier clearly in your application and ensure your overall budget ask falls within it:

 - Tier 1: under $50,000: Suited to focused, well-scoped projects such as pilot studies, evaluations, replications, or extensions of existing work. These applications undergo a streamlined review.

 - Tier 2: under $200,000: Suited to substantial projects requiring dedicated personnel time, meaningful compute, or data collection. Reviewed with proportionally greater attention to the budget breakdown and implementation plan.

 - Tier 3: under $500,000: Reserved for ambitious, multi-component research programs. These applications receive the highest level of scrutiny: reviewers will expect a detailed justification of each spend category, a clear account of team capacity to execute at this scale, and milestones against which progress can be assessed.

The level of review scrutiny scales with the size of the ask, so applicants should request the smallest budget that credibly supports the proposed work.



 


RESEARCH AGENDA

 

We are interested in submissions in the following area:

1. Measuring AI’s impact on labor

 - How should we measure AI’s effect on real economic and labor outcomes — and what methodologies are up to the task?

 - To what extent do benchmark scores map onto real economic outcomes?

 - What is the right methodology for measuring AI’s impact on labor outcomes (employment, wages, task composition)?

 - How does occupational exposure to AI evolve over time, and how can novel datasets improve its measurement?



2. Human–AI collaboration and productivity

 - How do humans actually work with AI systems, and when does that collaboration make them more productive?

 - What is the efficiency gain of human experts when paired with AI models, and under what conditions?

 - How can we measure the “review cost” that model outputs impose on humans — the time and effort spent checking, correcting, and verifying AI work?

 - Which collaboration patterns improve output quality rather than merely output volume?



3. Enterprise adoption and returns

 - What does AI adoption look like inside organizations, and what returns does it generate?

 - How are organizations actually using AI, and how is that usage changing?

 - How can the effect of AI and agent deployments be measured causally, rather than through self-report or correlation?

 - What are the right enterprise-level variables for quantifying AI-driven productivity gains?



 


ELIGIBILITY

 

 - Researchers at universities and non-profit research organizations, as well as public benefit corporations and small startups (<20 people) that do not sell AI training data. Awards are made to the researcher’s institution.

 - Applicants must be based in the United States or the United Kingdom

We expect grantees to publish a paper, an open dataset, a public methodology, or a tool the field can use, released under an open license that permits commercial use.

 


TIMELINE

 

 - Application deadline: November 27, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (UTC−8)

 - Notification to applicants: by December 18, 2026

Late or incomplete applications will not be reviewed. All applicants will be notified of the outcome whether or not they are shortlisted.

 
 


HOW TO APPLY

We invite interested researchers to submit a brief Expression of Interest (EOI) before preparing a full proposal. The EOI should be ~1–3 pages and include:

 - Research question and background (max 250 words): What are you trying to do? State your objective in plain language, with minimal jargon. How is this problem addressed today, and what are the limits of current practice? Who cares: if you succeed, what difference will it make, and to whom?

 - Project proposal (max 400 words): Concrete technical and implementation detail: your approach, methods, datasets, models, compute, and evaluation plan.

 - Novelty (max 200 words): What is new in your approach relative to existing and ongoing work, and why do you believe it will succeed where current practice falls short?

 - Risks (max 150 words): What are the main technical and execution risks, and how will you mitigate or detect them early?

 - Team (max 100 words; if the team is large, up to 200): The researchers on the project and their relevant background and prior work.

 - Proposed outcomes and timeline: Expected deliverables (papers, artifacts, datasets, tools) and key milestones, including how long the work will take. Include the mid-term and final “exams”: the checkpoints and success criteria by which we will know whether the project is on track and succeeds.

 - Budget overview: How much will it cost? Provide a specific overall budget ask, your budget tier (see Budget Categories), and a breakdown by spend category (e.g., personnel, compute, data, travel/other).
   
   - Other sources of funding for this project should be clearly identified in the proposal budget




GUIDANCE FOR APPLICANTS.

 - Strong EOIs are specific rather than high-level: they name the methods, systems, and evaluation criteria they will use, and they engage directly with existing literature and ongoing efforts rather than describing the problem space in general terms.

 - The EOI should briefly establish the PI’s (and key team members’) relevant background and prior work; proposals without demonstrated expertise in the research area are rarely competitive. Researchers with experience with agentic evaluation, RL environments, and post-training are encouraged to apply

 - Proposals that duplicate work already being pursued by many other groups are unlikely to advance unless they offer a clearly differentiated angle.

jobs.title: Data & Analytics Advisor - Operations
jobs.jd: CURRENT EMPLOYEES - Please apply using "Jobs Hub" in Workday. This career site is for external applicants only. The Advisor, Operations Data & Analytics is a senior individual contributor and strategic partner to Upstream Operations, turning operational and production data into decisions that improve field performance and efficiency. This role owns the analytics stack used daily by Drilling, Completions, Production, and Production Accounting — from Snowflake data models through Spotfire and/or Power BI dashboards to Streamlit applications deployed in the field. The ideal candidate pairs deep upstream oil & gas fluency with strong data engineering and visualization skills. Job Duties and Responsibilities : Include but are not limited to: Own the end-to-end reporting stack for Upstream Operations, from source-system ingestion through curated Snowflake models to the final dashboard. Develop and optimize Snowflake data models, SQL, and automated Python workflows, replacing manual and spreadsheet-based reporting. Build and administer advanced Spotfire and/or Power BI content, including reusable datasets and templates that enable self-service. Develop and deploy Streamlit applications that put analytics and operational tools directly in the hands of field and office users. Build and maintain reporting against ProCount, WellView, SiteView, Actenum, Ignition, XSPOC, and SCADA/historian platforms. Partner with Operations, Engineering, and Operations Technology to scope business needs, prioritize requests, and steward consistent KPI and data definitions. Define development and documentation standards, and present findings and recommendations to Operations leadership. Required Qualifications : Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a related field — or equivalent professional experience. Seven (7+) or more years in data reporting or analytics, including significant experience supporting upstream oil & gas operations. Expert-level SQL, including window functions, CTEs, and query performance tuning against large datasets. Hands-on experience building data models in a cloud data warehouse — Snowflake strongly preferred. Expert-level proficiency in Spotfire and/or Power BI, building dashboards for field and executive audiences. Strong Python for analysis and automation, and demonstrated ability to deploy analytical web applications — Streamlit preferred. Deep familiarity with upstream workflows and data from ProCount, WellView, SiteView, and SCADA sources. Ability to independently scope, prioritize, and deliver projects with limited direction. Preferred Qualifications: Streamlit in Snowflake, Snowpark, and Snowflake tasks, streams, or dynamic tables. Hands-on experience with upstream operational applications and their underlying data structures. Effective use of AI coding assistants to accelerate SQL, Python, and dashboard development, including judgment about when generated code requires review and validation.
